'''Ezra Buzzington''' is an American [[character actor]] in film and television. A figure in [[underground cinema]], Buzzington is also the founder of the Seattle Fringe Festival and co-founder of the [[New York International Fringe Festival]].

== Career ==
With over 70 film credits (and dozens of television appearances), Buzzington has been referred to as "the Dennis Hopper of underground cinema". He has played characters ranging from "Weird Al the Waiter" in ''[[Ghost World (film)|Ghost World]]'' to "Goggle" (a mutant) in ''[[The Hills Have Eyes (2006 film)|The Hills Have Eyes]]'' and Tudley in the Crime thriller film ''[[The Chair (2015 film)|The Chair]]''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.dreadcentral.com/news/94482/teaser-screams-emanate-from-the-chair/|title=Teaser Screams Emanate from The Chair|first=Steve|last=Barton|date=March 25, 2015}}</ref> He also appeared in the Academy Award-winning Best Picture ''[[The Artist (film)|The Artist]]'' and the Oscar-nominated ''[[The Fabelmans]]''. He has worked with directors [[David Fincher]] (twice), [[Alexandre Aja]] (twice), [[Terry Zwigoff]] (twice), [[Rob Zombie]] (twice), [[David Slade]] (four times), [[Steven Spielberg]], [[Christopher Nolan]], [[Paul Thomas Anderson]], [[George Clooney]], [[Clint Eastwood]] and the [[Farrelly Brothers]] (also twice). He was a series regular in the role of Oswald Eisengrim on [[NBC]]'s ''[[Crossbones (TV series)|Crossbones]]'' opposite [[John Malkovich]]'s [[Blackbeard]], recurred on NBC's ''[[Law & Order True Crime]]'' as DDA Elliot Alhadeff, recurred on [[American Broadcasting Company|ABC]]'s ''[[The Middle (TV series)|The Middle]]'' as the hard of hearing co-worker of [[Neil Flynn]]'s character, starred in an episode of [[CBS]]'s ''[[How I Met Your Mother]]'' and made several appearances on ''[[Justified (TV series)|Justified]]'' for [[FX (TV channel)|FX]].

He is the founder of the Seattle Fringe Festival,{{citation needed|date=October 2016}} co-founder of the [[New York International Fringe Festival]] with [[John Clancy (playwright)|John Clancy]] and Aaron Beall,{{citation needed|date=October 2016}} and an advisor for the [[Hollywood Fringe Festival]] during its first seven years.{{citation needed|date=October 2016}} He is also the creator of Theatrism, a metaphysical approach to theatrical staging.
